description: Held objects must not pass through walls, furniture, counters or the stove. Today every grabbable uses XRGrabInteractable MovementType Instantaneous (m_MovementType 2), which makes the Rigidbody kinematic and teleports it to the hand, so nothing blocks it. Add a runtime component that makes held objects physical while held, installed automatically on every grabbable so no scene or prefab edit is needed. Independent of FEAT-003 (different files), can run in parallel with it.
steps: Create Assets/Scripts/Common/HeldObjectPhysics.cs (+ .cs.meta with a new unique guid) in the LoveAtFirstBite.Runtime assembly. Component [DisallowMultipleComponent] [RequireComponent(typeof(Rigidbody), typeof(XRGrabInteractable))] following the style of PanSnap.cs (serialized m_ fields with tooltips, XML summary).

Behaviour: on selectEntered remember the original movementType and switch the XRGrabInteractable to VelocityTracking (physics driven, so the held Rigidbody collides with static colliders and is stopped by walls, counters, stove and furniture); tune velocityDamping / velocityScale / angularVelocityDamping / angularVelocityScale and tightenPosition / tightenRotation so the object follows the hand closely without jitter; on selectExited restore the original movementType. Keep ThrowOnDetach working. Set Rigidbody.collisionDetectionMode to ContinuousDynamic for non-kinematic bodies (thin objects: plates, knife, pan) and interpolation to Interpolate.

While held, call Physics.IgnoreCollision between every Collider of the held object (including child colliders such as Pan.prefab Colliders/Base, Wall, Handle) and the colliders of the player rig (the CharacterController and any non-trigger collider under the XROrigin / interactor hand objects), so a pan held close to the body is not blocked by the player's own capsule. Re-enable those collisions on release. Skip trigger colliders. Find the rig via FindFirstObjectByType<Unity.XR.CoreUtils.XROrigin>() at selection time (cache the collider list).

Add a static installer in the same file: [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.AfterSceneLoad)] that adds HeldObjectPhysics to every XRGrabInteractable in the loaded scene (FindObjectsByType<XRGrabInteractable>(FindObjectsInactive.Include, FindObjectsSortMode.None)) that has a non-kinematic-at-rest Rigidbody and a movementType of Instantaneous or Kinematic; skip objects that already have the component and skip interactables without a Rigidbody. Do not add it to knobs (Assets/Scripts/Stove/Knob.cs objects, which have no Rigidbody).

Check Pan.cs and PanSnap.cs behave correctly when the held pan is non-kinematic (Pan.cs sticks items with FixedJoint and checks isSelected; PanSnap.cs returns early while isSelected and when Body.isKinematic). Adjust only if something would break; the user confirmed the pan works well and its snap-to-burner behaviour must not regress. Also check Assets/Scripts/Slicing/KnifeSlicer.cs does not assume the knife is kinematic while held.

Add PlayMode tests in Assets/Scripts/Tests/PlayMode/HeldObjectPhysicsTests.cs following the structure of PanTests.cs: (a) installer adds the component to a grabbable with Instantaneous movement, (b) selecting switches the movement type to VelocityTracking and releasing restores Instantaneous, (c) player rig collision is ignored while held and restored after release. Tests must fail if the component is removed. Compile them with the FEAT-001 script (they cannot be executed while the Editor is open).
Update Documentation only if an existing doc lists pan/grab mechanics (optional, Romanian, one short paragraph).
acceptance_criteria: HeldObjectPhysics.cs and its .meta exist and the runtime and test sources compile with 0 errors using the FEAT-001 compile script
Held objects use VelocityTracking while selected and the original movement type is restored on release (covered by a PlayMode test)
Collisions between the held object and the player rig colliders are ignored while held and restored on release (covered by a PlayMode test)
Pan.cs and PanSnap.cs logic still compiles and no existing PlayMode test assumption (kinematic held pan) is broken; any needed change is documented in findings
verification: Run the FEAT-001 csc compile script for runtime and test sources and confirm 0 errors
Re-read HeldObjectPhysics.cs and the new tests and confirm each test would fail if the component logic were removed
findings:
RESULT: compile_check.ps1 reports TOTAL ERRORS: 0 (runtime, PlayMode, EditMode). Tests were NOT executed (Editor open). No git commit (sandbox).

FILES: new Assets/Scripts/Common/HeldObjectPhysics.cs (+.meta guid 4b9d2e7a15c34f08a6e1d3c7b0f82a64); new Assets/Scripts/Tests/PlayMode/HeldObjectPhysicsTests.cs (+.meta guid a37f0c5e82b14d69b5c2e9d4f1a60b83, 5 tests); edited Assets/Scripts/Tests/PlayMode/LoveAtFirstBite.Tests.PlayMode.asmdef (added references Unity.XR.Interaction.Toolkit and Unity.XR.CoreUtils, needed by the new tests; the asmdef has overrideReferences true).

BEHAVIOUR: on selectEntered it stores the original movementType and sets XRGrabInteractable.movementType = VelocityTracking. XRI 3.3.2 supports changing movementType while selected (UpdateCurrentMovementType does SetupRigidbodyDrop then SetupRigidbodyGrab), so the body becomes non-kinematic after the initial Instantaneous grab made it kinematic. On release (selectExited, only when no other hand still holds it) the original type is restored; ThrowOnDetach is untouched and works (XRI computes the throw from smoothed target velocity and applies it in Detach, which skips kinematic bodies, and the body is non-kinematic after Drop). Rigidbody set to ContinuousDynamic + Interpolate in Awake and on grab (non-kinematic bodies only, serialized toggle m_RobustBody). Rig collisions: on grab it finds the XROrigin (interactor parent first, FindFirstObjectByType fallback) and calls Physics.IgnoreCollision between every enabled non-trigger collider of the held object (children included) and every enabled non-trigger collider under the XROrigin (CharacterController, hand colliders). DEVIATION (improvement): after release a pair is only re-enabled once the two colliders' bounds no longer intersect (checked in FixedUpdate), so a pan dropped inside the player capsule is not shoved; pairs that do not overlap are restored immediately. Installer: public static int HeldObjectPhysics.InstallAll() (called from [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(AfterSceneLoad)]) adds the component to every XRGrabInteractable (inactive included) with a Rigidbody that is not kinematic and movementType Instantaneous or Kinematic; knobs have no Rigidbody so they are skipped. Objects instantiated after scene load (for example KnifeSlicer halves) are clones of an object that already has the component, so they keep it; the movement type is stored in a serialized hidden field so a clone made while the original is held restores correctly in Awake.

DEVIATIONS: tightenPosition / tightenRotation are not set: they only apply with smoothPosition/smoothRotation (off in this project) so they would have no effect. velocityDamping, velocityScale, angularVelocityDamping, angularVelocityScale are exposed and default to 1/1/1/1 (XRI defaults, full follow with no overshoot or jitter); these are not restored on release because they only affect VelocityTracking. No documentation change: no existing Documentation file lists pan/grab mechanics.

PAN / PANSNAP / KNIFE CHECK (no code change needed): Pan.CanStick rejects isSelected items, so a held (now non-kinematic) item is still never stuck, and Pan detaches stuck items on selectEntered as before. Pan never reads or writes its own isKinematic. PanSnap resets while m_Interactable.isSelected, and after release XRI restores isKinematic=false exactly as before, so snap timing is unchanged (its IsCalm speed thresholds are evaluated after the 0.1 s settle delay and after XRI applies the throw velocity). While held PanSnap does not run, so its Glide velocity writes never touch a held body. PanTests and PanSnapTests contain no XR, so they are unaffected (the installer only runs on scene load, not in those tests). KnifeSlicer measures its own speed from transform movement in FixedUpdate and uses a trigger collider, which works with a dynamic body; it does not assume kinematic. SetUpHalf rebuilds colliders and grab.colliders on cloned halves; the cloned HeldObjectPhysics is created with fresh runtime state and still works because XRGrabInteractable on the half is the same component set.

TESTS (HeldObjectPhysicsTests, cannot run now): TestInteractor : XRBaseInteractor (no input, keepSelectedTargetValid true) selected and released through XRInteractionManager.SelectEnter/SelectExit with IXRSelectInteractor/IXRSelectInteractable casts (the XRBase* overloads are obsolete and cause CS0619). Tests: installer adds component (and not twice), installer skips kinematic bodies, select switches to VelocityTracking with a non-kinematic body and release restores Instantaneous, rig collision ignored while held and restored after release (rig far away), pair stays ignored after release while overlapping the rig and is restored after the rig moves away. All assert on HeldObjectPhysics state or behaviour, so they fail if the component is removed (Install returns null / movement type stays Instantaneous). The XROrigin created by tests logs two LogWarning messages (no camera floor offset, no main camera) which do not fail tests. Not covered by a test: an actual wall blocking a held object (would need XRI update loop timing that cannot be validated while the Editor is open). Please run PlayMode tests in the Editor once and check in the scene that the held pan stops at walls and the stove.
